newsitem.title: USA: GM unit wins FAA contract worth up to $100mln.
newsitem.headline: GM unit wins FAA contract worth up to $100mln.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration on Monday awarded an air traffic control modernization contract to a unit of General Motors Corp. that could be worth up to $100 million.

Hughes Information Technology Systems, based in Upper Marlboro, Maryland, was awarded the contract. The unit is part of the Hughes Aircraft Co., which is part of Hughes Electronics Corp., a wholly owned GM company.
The FAA said the contract was for $40 million, with two two-year options of $30 million each.

It said the Hughes unit would provide technical integration of the National Airspace System Infrastructure Management System (MIMS) to increase the productivity of the agency's 30,000-plus facilities and pieces of equipment coast-to-coast.
The FAA said the centralized management system would consolidate previously separate efforts and result in greater management efficiency and budget savings.
